member: Dalia - Cooperative Use and Produce Preservation Specialist
message:
Amara, Baraka and Chidi, one tonne moves by hand in crate loads fitting racks and aisle.

Single-person carry is 20 kg per crate, where kg means kilogrammes, so 50 crates times 20 kg equals 1000 kg, using 600 by 400 mm footprint, where mm means millimetres, in the stacking crate (E36 crate), and 10.6 cubic metre inner volume at 27 percent fill in the chamber simulation (E44 simulation), within 23 kg ideal limit in the lifting guidance (E49 guidance). 20 kg is airport luggage, so members can handle it.

Rot slows by outside sorting and air moving around vented crates with rotation. Remove damaged and diseased items before loading, rest moves First-In First-Out, where First-In First-Out (FIFO) means oldest sold first, per sorting to eliminate defects (E46 practices) and high-humidity storage (E19 practices), with crate air gaps and fan flow in the cold room sketch (E32 sketch). Daily checks stop one bad crate spreading.

Box stays food safe by washdown to drain, no heavy lift. Washable food-grade vented crates in the crate evidence (E52 crate) and crate listing (E53 listing) drain through floor drain in the cold room sketch (E32), and 2.04 kilopascal floor pressure from one tonne in the pressure calculation (E43 calculation) shows spreaders carry load, members lift only one crate. I am not ready, because rack guard height and door operation with Chidi and field-heat waiting time with Baraka remain to fix.
